deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page). k is the subfield ('Unterkörper') of absolute degree nu with discriminant D_U. K is the upper field ('Oberkörper') with relative degree mu over k, absolute degree n = nu*mu, and discriminant D_0. By a lemma, there is a rational or k-integer c prime to D_U and fixed elements xi_1..xi_mu of K (built from powers of a generator epsilon) with the following property: for every integer omega of K, c*omega = tau_1 xi_1 + ... + tau_mu xi_mu with tau_i integers of k. Take an integral basis omega_1..omega_n of K. Then det(c omega_j^{(i)}) for i,j = 1..n equals (up to sign) c^n D_0^{1/2}. The page text writes the power of c as c^{(n n-1)/2} or similar, partly struck through; see errors.

THIS PAGE. Goal: D_0 is divisible by D_U^mu.

Step 1. Write c omega_1 = tau_1 xi_1 + ... + tau_mu xi_mu, c omega_2 = sigma_1 xi_1 + ..., ..., c omega_n = kappa_1 xi_1 + ... + kappa_mu xi_mu. Rows 2..n of the determinant contain the conjugates of row 1.

Step 2. The determinant is multilinear in its columns. Expanding each column into its mu summands writes it as a sum of determinants. In each of these, every column has the form (rho^{(i)} xi_k^{(i)})_i for a single k, with rho in k. So each term is det[tau'_1 xi_1, ..., tau'_nu xi_1, sigma'_1 xi_2, ..., kappa'_nu xi_mu] after reordering columns (sign only).

Step 3 (why each xi_k occurs in exactly nu columns). Suppose nu+1 columns carry the same xi_1, say tau'_1 xi_1, ..., tau'_{nu+1} xi_1. Since [k:Q] = nu, there are rational integers a_1..a_{nu+1}, not all 0, with a_1 tau'_1 + ... + a_{nu+1} tau'_{nu+1} = 0. The same relation holds for all conjugates, so the columns are dependent and the determinant vanishes. There are n = nu*mu columns and mu values of k, so every surviving term has exactly nu columns for each xi_k.

Step 4 (generalised Laplace expansion). Expand along the mu column blocks of width nu: for each block choose nu rows, with complementary row sets across blocks. In the minor for block k with rows r_1..r_nu, factor xi_k^{(r)} out of each row. The minor becomes prod_r xi_k^{(r)} times det(tau'_j^{(r_s)}).

Step 5. The n conjugates of an element of k take only nu distinct values, one per embedding of k.
- If two chosen rows restrict to the same embedding of k, two rows are equal and det(tau'^{(r_s)}_j) = 0.
- Otherwise the rows are a permutation of the nu conjugates of k. Then det(tau'_j^{(s)}) = det(M) * D_U^{1/2} (up to sign), where M is the integer matrix expressing the tau' in an integral basis of k. So it is divisible by D_U^{1/2}.

Step 6. Each Laplace term is a product of mu such minors, so it is divisible by D_U^{mu/2}. Hence c^n D_0^{1/2} is divisible by D_U^{mu/2}. Squaring, and using that c is prime to D_U, D_0 is divisible by D_U^mu.

IMPLICIT (mine): Step 6 needs the leftover factors prod xi_k^{(r)} to be integral, or at least to have denominators prime to D_U. It also needs divisibility to be read in the ring of algebraic integers, with the square taken at the end to return to rational integers.
errors: Power of c: det(c*omega_j^{(i)}) = c^n det(omega_j^{(i)}), so the factor should be c^n (squared: c^{2n}), not c^{n(n-1)/2}. The page writes 'c^{(nn-1)/..}' with part struck out. The slip is harmless because c is prime to D_U and only that is used.

Unstated assumption: the cofactors prod xi_k^{(r)} must be algebraic integers, or have denominators prime to D_U, for the divisibility to transfer. The previous page suggests xi_mu may carry a fractional coefficient like a/p. The argument needs either integral xi's or denominators prime to D_U, which the choice of c seems meant to ensure. This is not made explicit on this page.
Step 6 uses divisibility by the irrational D_U^{1/2} inside the ring of algebraic integers without comment. This is standard but tacit.
Minor: 'In der That wählt man etwa tau_1 xi_1 ...' should refer to tau'_1 xi_1, ..., tau'_{nu+1} xi_1.

results.what: For a tower Q < k < K with [K:k] = mu, the discriminant of K is divisible by the mu-th power of the discriminant of k.
results.modern_name: Tower (transitivity) formula for discriminants, d_K = d_k^{[K:k]} * N_{k/Q}(d_{K/k}), in its weak divisibility form
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind / Kronecker (1880s); systematically in Hilbert's Zahlbericht (1897)

results.what: Proof technique: expand the discriminant determinant multilinearly over a relative 'basis' xi_k. Kill terms with more than nu columns per xi_k via Q-linear dependence of nu+1 elements of k. Then apply the Laplace expansion in nu-column blocks, whose minors are 0 or multiples of D_U^{1/2}.
results.modern_name: Determinant/Laplace-expansion proof of the discriminant divisibility in towers

deep.surprise_reason: The divisibility d_k^{[K:k]} | d_K is standard 19th-century algebraic number theory and appears in Hilbert's own Zahlbericht. This page is a student-notebook-style proof of a known fact. The determinant-expansion route is somewhat elementary and unusual but not historically significant.

checkable.asserts: Discriminant of Q(2^(1/4)), whose ring of integers is Z[2^(1/4)] (Eisenstein at 2), is -2048.
D_0 = -2048 is divisible by D_U^mu = 8^2 for k = Q(sqrt2), mu = 2.
For K = Q(zeta_8) over k = Q(i): D_0 = 256 is divisible by (-4)^2.
A conjugate determinant of an integral basis of k squares to D_U (here 8), i.e. nu x nu minors are multiples of D_U^(1/2).

Illustrative only: with nu = 2, three elements 1, sqrt2, 3*sqrt2 of k are Q-dependent (3*sqrt2 - 3*sqrt2 = 0). Two columns built from them with a common xi are proportional, so such terms vanish (cf. Step 3).

transcription_corrections: Line 'In der That wählt man etwa tau_1 xi_1 .. tau'_{nu+1} xi_1': the first entry should be tau'_1 xi_1 (primed).
'indem du ersten aus den ersten nu Verticalreihen' should read 'indem man zuerst aus den ersten nu Verticalreihen'.
Factor matrix rows are tau'^{(nu_1)}_1..tau'^{(nu_1)}_nu, tau'^{(nu_2)}_1..tau'^{(nu_2)}_nu, ..., tau'^{(nu_nu)}_1..tau'^{(nu_nu)}_nu, with row indices nu_1..nu_nu the selected conjugates.

Margin text 'den Faktor ... ginten Werth ... ist sind' is the line-wrapped continuation 'welcher, da die conjugirten Werthe von tau nur nu verschieden sind, entweder = 0 oder durch D_U^{1/2} theilbar wird'.
'i^{(n-1)/..} D_0^{1/2}' is better read as 'c^{(nn-1)/2}' or 'c^{...}' with a struck-out exponent, i.e. c^{...} D_0^{1/2} is divisible by D_U^{mu/2}. The mathematically correct power is c^n.
